short: ISO 14001 is the ISO requirements standard for an environmental management system; the current edition, ISO 14001:2026, was published on 15 April 2026, and it is held as a certificate issued by a certification body.
title: ISO 14001, Environmental Management Systems
subtitle: The ISO requirements standard for an environmental management system, now in its 2026 edition
body_html:
What ISO 14001 is

ISO 14001 sets the requirements for an environmental management system that an organization can use to improve its environmental performance. It is written by ISO/TC 207, subcommittee SC 1. The current edition is ISO 14001:2026, the fourth, published on 15 April 2026. It replaced ISO 14001:2015 and its 2024 climate action amendment. ISO Open Data also lists a second amendment to the 2015 edition that stopped at draft stage.

ISO describes it as a way to manage environmental responsibilities systematically, as a contribution to the environmental side of sustainability. It applies to any organization and to the environmental aspects of its activities, products and services that it can control or influence, seen across their life cycle.

What it covers

  • Improving environmental performance.
  • Meeting compliance obligations.
  • Setting and achieving environmental objectives.

How conformity is shown

ISO publishes the standard and sells its text. ISO Open Data, the dataset ISO publishes for reuse, records the edition, the committee and the scope, and that is what this page is built from. It does not record who holds a certificate. A certificate against a requirements standard like this one is issued by a certification body after an audit, and it names that body, the edition, the scope and the dates.

What a claim does not mean

ISO 14001 sets no environmental performance criteria. A certified organization has an audited system for managing its environmental effects; the certificate does not say its emissions, water use or energy use are low. ISO also says a claim of conformity is not acceptable unless every requirement is built into the system and met without exclusion.

ISO 14001 in data centers

For a data center, the environmental aspects in scope usually include energy, refrigerants, water, diesel generators, waste and noise. A certificate shows these are managed under an audited system at the sites it names. Energy performance has its own standard, ISO 50001, and the European programmes, the EU Code of Conduct for Data Centres and the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact, set targets that ISO 14001 does not.

  • Scope. A certificate covers named sites, services or activities. One site certified does not mean every site the operator runs is certified.
  • Edition. The certificate names the edition it was audited against. A certificate issued before the 2026 edition names ISO 14001:2015.
  • Certification body and certificate number. These let a reader confirm the certificate with the body that issued it.
  • Dates. A certificate has an issue date and an expiry date.

Related standards

See also ISO 50001, LEED (which rates a building, not a management system) and the Standards and Frameworks hub.

Primary sources

  • ISO 14001:2026, ISO standard page (linked for readers; iso.org refuses automated readers, so the facts above come from ISO Open Data)
  • ISO Open Data, deliverables metadata: edition, publication date, committee and scope
